subject: translation-studies
intro: Translation studies leads to work across languages: professional translators and interpreters, editors who shape written text, and university teachers of languages and literature.

roles.title: Interpreters and Translators
roles.what: Interpret oral or sign language, or translate written text from one language into another, carrying meaning across cultures for legal, medical, literary and commercial clients while managing equivalence, register and accuracy.
roles.where: This is the course's core profession: the equivalence and meaning, translation techniques and specialised translation units, plus CAT tools, machine translation post-editing and the ATA error typology, are the working craft of the job.

roles.title: Editors
roles.what: Plan, coordinate, revise or edit written material for publication: review drafts, correct and polish text, check consistency and style, and decide what content serves its audience best.
roles.where: Source-text analysis, the literal-versus-free spectrum and the quality assessment and error typology unit train the judgement editors apply when revising text — including the translated manuscripts they shepherd to publication.

roles.title: Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach language and literature courses in languages other than English at colleges and universities, designing courses, leading classes and often researching linguistics or the literature of the language taught.
roles.where: The theory of what translation is and the comparative analysis of meaning across languages give you the deep bilingual literacy language teaching at university level demands, often after graduate study.
